title: Home Mortgage Loans: Adjustable-Rate Caps
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Adjustable-Rate Caps

Rate caps limit how far the note rate on an adjustable loan within Home Mortgage Loans can move. Three caps are published: one for the first change after the fixed period, one for every change after that, and one on the total rise above the starting rate across the life of the loan.

| Program | First-change cap (percentage points) | Later-change cap (percentage points) | Lifetime cap above the starting rate (percentage points) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7/6 SOFR Adjustable-Rate Mortgage | 5.00 | 1.00 | 5.00 |
| Conventional 15-Year Fixed Mortgage | not relevant — rate never adjusts | not relevant | not relevant |
| Conventional 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | not relevant — rate never adjusts | not relevant | not relevant |
| FHA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | not relevant — rate never adjusts | not relevant | not relevant |
| Jumbo 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | not relevant — rate never adjusts | not relevant | not relevant |
| VA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | not relevant — rate never adjusts | not relevant | not relevant |

## What each cap limits

- **First-change cap** — the largest amount, up or down, by which the rate may change at the first adjustment.
- **Later-change cap** — the largest amount by which the rate may change at any single adjustment after the first.
- **Lifetime cap** — the largest total increase over the starting rate that the note rate may ever reach.

## Points of judgement

**Could the first adjustment move the rate by six points?** No; the first-change cap is 5.00 points.

**After the first adjustment, can a single change exceed one point?** No; each later change is capped at 1.00 point.

**Hypothetical ceiling.** If an imagined adjustable loan had started at 6.000 percent, the lifetime cap would keep its rate at or below 11.000 percent, namely the starting rate increased by 5.00 points. The starting rate used here is an illustration, not a published rate.
